title: Dr. STONE Structured Question Bank
adaptationBoundary: TV anime continuity through Dr. STONE SCIENCE FUTURE episode 94, 'Ushers of an Exhilarating Future' (released June 25, 2026), including the Dr. STONE: Ryusui television special; excludes manga-only material and any unreleased or unverified sequel content.
notes: All 75 prompts are original wording and test one objectively checkable anime fact.
Episode numbering and release coverage were cross-checked against the released-episode list and Crunchyroll's official series/news pages.
Where science is discussed, explanations identify anime fictionalization or simplification rather than presenting it as established real-world science.
Source status is 'verified' for every item; no manga-only revelation or unreleased material is used.

questions.prompt: What span of time does Senku say has passed since the petrification event?
questions.explanation: The opening episode establishes that humanity has been stone for roughly 3,700 years.

questions.prompt: Who is the first person Senku revives in the Stone World?
questions.explanation: Senku revives his friend Taiju before attempting to recruit anyone else.

questions.prompt: What cave-derived chemical does Senku identify as the key starting material for revival fluid?
questions.explanation: The anime identifies nitric acid from the cave as the essential starting point; the revival formula is an anime simplification, not a complete real-world method for dissolving petrified humans.

questions.prompt: What does Taiju keep counting while petrified?
questions.explanation: Taiju maintains consciousness by counting seconds throughout his petrification.

questions.prompt: Why does Senku revive Tsukasa so urgently?
options: To fight a pride of lions
questions.explanation: A lion attack leaves Senku and Taiju needing Tsukasa's exceptional physical strength.

questions.prompt: What kind of people does Tsukasa say he wants to revive first?
questions.explanation: Tsukasa's ideology favors a world revived without the adults he associates with the old corrupt society.

questions.prompt: How does Senku signal that the Kingdom of Science is active?
questions.explanation: Senku uses a column of smoke to announce his presence and draw Tsukasa's attention.

questions.prompt: What valuable material is found in the cave later called the Cave of Miracles?
questions.explanation: Sulfur is one of the cave resources that makes gunpowder and later chemical work possible.

source.title: Where Two Million Years Have Gone

questions.prompt: What is the name of the settled community that Senku encounters?
questions.explanation: Kohaku's home is Ishigami Village, whose name honors Byakuya Ishigami.

source.title: Where Two Million Years Have Gone

questions.prompt: What invention eventually gives the Kingdom of Science two-way long-distance voice communication?
questions.explanation: The team builds cell phones to create a communications network across the Stone World.

questions.prompt: What illness is Ruri suffering from when Senku first meets her?
questions.explanation: Ruri is gravely ill with pneumonia, motivating the search for the sulfa drug.

questions.prompt: Who is Byakuya Ishigami to Senku?
questions.explanation: Byakuya adopted Senku and later became one of the astronauts stranded after the petrification.

questions.prompt: What does the Village Games winner gain the right to do?
options: Become village chief and marry Ruri
questions.explanation: The games are held to choose Ruri's husband and the next village chief.

questions.prompt: What is the main subject of Byakuya's hundred tales?
options: The history and survival of humanity
questions.explanation: The hundred tales preserve knowledge and the story of humanity for descendants of the astronauts.

source.title: A Hundred Nights and a Thousand Skies

questions.prompt: Who leads the Empire of Might as its founder?
questions.explanation: Tsukasa establishes the opposing faction known as the Empire of Might.

questions.prompt: Which seasoning does Senku prioritize when recreating ramen?
questions.explanation: Salt is the key seasoning Senku seeks for the ramen project.

questions.prompt: Which mineral does Senku use as the magnetic material for early electrical experiments?
questions.explanation: Magnetite supplies the magnetic material for the first electrical experiments; the anime then simplifies the engineering sequence for storytelling.

source.title: Let There Be the Light of Science

questions.prompt: What is Gen Asagiri's profession before the petrification?
questions.explanation: Gen introduces himself as a mentalist and uses performance psychology to read and influence people.

questions.prompt: What medicine does Senku make for Ruri?
questions.explanation: The Kingdom of Science synthesizes a sulfa drug to treat Ruri's pneumonia.

questions.prompt: What job do Kinro and Ginro perform in Ishigami Village?
questions.explanation: The brothers serve as the village's guards and enforce its rules.

questions.prompt: Who wins the Village Games and becomes the village chief?
questions.explanation: Senku wins the tournament and becomes chief, although the position is a means to reach Ruri's medicine ingredients.

source.title: The Culmination of Two Million Years

questions.prompt: Which warrior is identified as Tsukasa's right-hand fighter?
questions.explanation: Hyoga is Tsukasa's most trusted spear-wielding lieutenant at this stage of the story.

questions.prompt: What machine does Senku build to begin the modern energy age?
questions.explanation: Senku builds a steam engine, the power source for the later mobile laboratory.

questions.prompt: Who is Ishigami Village's master craftsperson?
questions.explanation: Kaseki is the elderly craftsman whose skill makes precision construction possible.

questions.prompt: What metal is hidden in the treasure that makes large-scale revival fluid possible?
questions.explanation: The treasure contains platinum, which lets the Kingdom of Science make nitric acid continuously.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the cell-phone network in the first Stone Wars plan?
options: To communicate and coordinate across enemy territory
To replace the village's water supply
questions.explanation: The network provides secure long-distance communication for the Kingdom's strategy.

questions.prompt: Who performs the voice imitation used in the Lillian broadcast?
questions.explanation: Gen impersonates Lillian's voice to make the broadcast believable.

questions.prompt: What is the name of Tsukasa's faction?
questions.explanation: Tsukasa's followers form the Empire of Might.

questions.prompt: What does Senku use to maintain a communication link with the opposing side?
questions.explanation: The cell phone network lets Senku speak with allies and opponents during the Stone Wars.

questions.prompt: What does Yuzuriha secretly do for the Kingdom of Science during the war?
questions.explanation: Yuzuriha uses her extraordinary craft skills to restore statues without revealing the operation.

questions.prompt: How does Gen help make the Kingdom's fake Lillian broadcast convincing?
questions.explanation: Gen's vocal imitation supplies the voice that makes the radio deception work.

questions.prompt: What vehicle does the Kingdom of Science use for its decisive assault?
questions.explanation: Steam Gorilla is the armored vehicle used in the attack on the Empire's base.

questions.prompt: What is Yuzuriha's main wartime task after joining the Kingdom's operation?
questions.explanation: Yuzuriha repairs statues so the defeated Empire can be revived without losing its people.

questions.prompt: Who betrays Tsukasa during the final Stone Wars confrontation?
questions.explanation: Hyoga turns on Tsukasa because he wants power for himself.

questions.prompt: Which pair finally defeats Hyoga in the Stone Wars climax?
questions.explanation: Senku and Tsukasa cooperate to overcome Hyoga, combining science with Tsukasa's strength.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the Kingdom of Science's ocean-going ship?
questions.explanation: The crew names its science vessel Perseus.

questions.prompt: Who is revived specifically to captain the ocean voyage?
questions.explanation: Ryusui is revived because his pre-petrification sailing experience makes him the needed captain.

questions.prompt: What invention lets Senku, Ryusui, and Chrome survey the changed coastline from above?
questions.explanation: The hot-air balloon allows them to map the modern coastline and search for the oil field.

questions.prompt: What does Ryusui introduce to turn his greed into a formal market?
questions.explanation: Ryusui creates money and a market so goods and labor can be traded.

questions.prompt: What word repeats in the mysterious broadcast heard at sea?
questions.explanation: The unexplained ocean transmission repeatedly says 'WHY,' creating the next major mystery.

questions.prompt: What is the petrification device called in the Treasure Island storyline?
questions.explanation: The characters call the petrification device a Medusa.

questions.prompt: What does Soyuz's remembered name ultimately identify him as?
options: A former Kingdom of Science captain
questions.explanation: Soyuz's recovered memories connect him to the people of Treasure Island and its ruler.

source.title: Ray of Despair, Ray of Hope

questions.prompt: What is the key power source found inside each Medusa unit?
questions.explanation: The device's core is diamond-based; the anime's mechanism is fictionalized technology, not established science.

questions.prompt: What does Ibara use as the island's ultimate weapon against the intruders?
questions.explanation: Ibara controls the Medusa and uses its petrification effect to dominate Treasure Island.

questions.prompt: What do Ginro and Suika manage to escape with during the island climax?
questions.explanation: Ginro and Suika escape the ship with the mobile lab while the struggle for control of the Medusa unfolds.

questions.prompt: What is the true purpose of the New America City expedition?
options: Secure corn for mass revival fluid
Build a new village chief's palace
Capture every Medusa on the moon
questions.explanation: The American journey is driven by the need for corn, which can support large-scale revival-fluid production.

questions.prompt: Which character agrees to train Matsukaze after being revived?
questions.explanation: Hyoga accepts the training role in exchange for the right to choose two people to revive.

questions.prompt: What do corn-feeding moths help Senku locate?
questions.explanation: The moths' food source points the team toward the enemy's cornfield.

questions.prompt: Who is the scientist leading the hostile American colony?
questions.explanation: Dr. Xeno leads the American colony and becomes Senku's scientific rival.

questions.prompt: What industrial process does Xeno's colony use to produce gunpowder at scale?
questions.explanation: Xeno has built a Haber-Bosch plant; the episode presents this as an industrial fact, though the wider war technology remains anime fiction.

questions.prompt: Who is sent to infiltrate Senku's group and identify the real scientist?
questions.explanation: Luna is placed near the crew as an informant for Stanley and Xeno.

questions.prompt: What is Xeno's personal connection to young Senku?
options: He once mentored Senku by correspondence
He was Senku's rival at school
questions.explanation: Xeno answered Senku's childhood rocket questions and helped ignite his scientific ambition.

questions.prompt: What material mixture does Senku use as an improvised bullet-resistant vest?
questions.explanation: Senku combines starch and water into a viscous protective layer; the scene is an improvised anime application, not a complete real-world armor recipe.

questions.prompt: What does Chelsea contribute to the plan for crossing South America?
options: A shortcut route and motorcycle idea
questions.explanation: Chelsea's geographical knowledge suggests the overland shortcut and motivates the motorcycle build.

questions.prompt: What natural material is collected to make motorcycle tires?
questions.explanation: The team taps rubber trees and processes the latex into tires.

questions.prompt: Who analyzes the recovered Medusa as a master watchmaker?
questions.explanation: Joel's watchmaking skill lets the Corn City team dismantle and study the device.

questions.prompt: What does Hyoga do when Suika is blown from the ropeway?
options: He helps pull her to safety
questions.explanation: Hyoga assists Kohaku and Suika, showing that his reform is genuine.

questions.prompt: What causes many of the Medusa units in the Amazon to be unusable?
options: Their diamond cores are damaged or charred
Their shells are made of wood
questions.explanation: The team finds dead batteries and damaged diamond cores; the device technology itself is fictionalized.

questions.prompt: What is Chrome's proposed battlefield strategy at Araxá?
options: Petrify both armies and revive the Kingdom later
Hide the Perseus in the Pacific
questions.explanation: Chrome proposes using a revived Medusa to petrify both forces and let a distant ally revive their side.

questions.prompt: What does Xeno secretly send to Stanley before the final confrontation?
options: A coded message revealing their location
questions.explanation: Xeno betrays the Kingdom's position by transmitting a coded message to Stanley.

questions.prompt: What is Senku's immediate objective when Science Future's final cour begins?
options: Resume the plan to fly to the moon
Return to the Stone Formula cave
questions.explanation: The final cour resumes the long-term plan to reach the moon and confront the source of the petrification mystery.

questions.prompt: Which person is chosen to teach Sai the mathematics needed for advanced computing?
questions.explanation: Chrome asks Sai for mathematical help, and Sai becomes the key mathematical expert for the computer project.

source.title: The Universe Is Written in the Language of Mathematics

questions.prompt: What does Senku build to automate calculations and support the rocket program?
questions.explanation: The Kingdom builds a computer as a major step toward modern computation and aerospace engineering.

questions.prompt: What kind of memory does Senku recreate for the computer?
questions.explanation: Senku uses tiny magnetized cores to encode binary information in magnetic-core memory.

questions.prompt: Why does Senku plan a one-way lunar mission at first?
options: There is not enough time to build a return-capable rocket
questions.explanation: The immediate deadline forces a one-way design, leaving the astronauts to petrify themselves until a future rescue.

questions.prompt: What power infrastructure is needed to produce the aluminum for the rocket?
questions.explanation: Senku says the aluminum process needs massive electricity, leading the team to the planned hydroelectric dam.

questions.prompt: What does the successful Senku-7 mission allow Kohaku to locate?
options: An unnatural structure on the Moon
questions.explanation: Satellite images let Kohaku's exceptional vision identify the unnatural lunar structure associated with Why-Man.

questions.prompt: Which three roles are selected for the lunar crew?
questions.explanation: The mission needs a pilot, a scientist, and a warrior to handle flight, investigation, and danger.

questions.prompt: Who ultimately replaces Ryusui as the planned lunar pilot?
questions.explanation: Ryusui admits Stanley is the superior pilot and marksman for the lunar mission.

questions.prompt: What material does Senku use to make the astronauts' spacesuits?
questions.explanation: Vinyl is used for the improvised spacesuits in the anime's rebuilt technology chain.

questions.prompt: How does Ryusui help steer the lunar module after the reaction wheel is unavailable?
options: He spins himself as a human reaction wheel
questions.explanation: Ryusui straps himself to a disk and spins, supplying angular momentum; the scene is an anime workaround for a real spacecraft-control problem.

questions.prompt: What does Why-Man turn out to be on the Moon?
questions.explanation: The explorers discover that Why-Man is a colony of Medusas communicating together.

questions.prompt: Which animals were the first targets of Why-Man's petrification experiments?
questions.explanation: Why-Man says it first tested its petrification on swallows before targeting humanity.

questions.prompt: What philosophy does Why-Man claim petrification offers intelligent life?
questions.explanation: Why-Man presents petrification as a route to eternal existence, which Senku rejects in favor of continued scientific progress.

questions.prompt: What project does Senku reveal after the lunar conflict is resolved?
questions.explanation: The ending reveals that Senku and the scientists are attempting to build a time machine to prevent the first petrification.
